Dispatch.description: How a rate-driven traffic group's arrivals reach its connections

oneOf.description:
Every connection runs its own share of the group's arrivals and sends
them itself; an arrival due while its connection's pipeline is full
waits for that connection (default)

Every thread runs one arrival process, its share of the group's rate,
and sends each arrival on the connection idle longest; an arrival due
while no connection is idle waits for the first to free up and counts
as a late send

NtcpAfXdp.description:
The network interface of backend "af_xdp"

Each worker thread that runs ntcp traffic groups gets one AF_XDP socket on
one queue of the interface and its own IPv4 address. An XDP program hands
the threads' addresses (and ARP for them) to their sockets and passes the
rest of the traffic to the kernel, which keeps its own address on the
interface. The threads share one ARP table.

gateway.description: Router for destinations outside that network

ntcp's own IPv4 address for each worker thread that runs ntcp traffic
groups, in ascending thread-id order; not the kernel's addresses

mode.description:
XDP attach mode: "native" (in the driver) or "generic" (any
interface, slower)

prefix_len.description: Prefix length of the on-link network of `local_ips`

NtcpDpdk.description:
The DPDK port of backend "dpdk"

Each worker thread that runs ntcp traffic groups gets one queue pair of
the port and its own IPv4 address, steered to its queue by a flow rule.
The threads share one ARP table. The port is not isolated: it receives
all of the device's traffic, so the kernel no longer sees the device's
traffic for other addresses while xylem runs (mlx5 VFs: bifurcated).

SamplingPolicy.description: Sampling policy configuration for latency measurement

oneOf.description: Disable latency sampling entirely (still counts bytes/requests)

Uniform random sample of at most `max_samples` latencies per entry.
Each latency is first kept with probability `rate`; the kept latencies
are reservoir-sampled, so the stored samples are a uniform sample of
every kept latency, not the first ones. Mean, min, max and standard
deviation are computed from every kept latency.

max_samples.description: Maximum number of samples to store

oneOf.description:
Zero sampling: record every latency (unlimited storage)
WARNING: Can consume large amounts of memory for high-throughput workloads

DDSketch: Distributed quantile sketch with relative-error guarantees
Memory-efficient and fully mergeable across traffic groups

max_bins.description: Maximum number of bins (in steps of 128)

oneOf.description:
T-Digest: Adaptive clustering sketch optimized for extreme tail percentiles
Better accuracy than DDSketch for p999+, fully mergeable

compression.description:
Positive compression parameter (higher = more accurate, more memory)
Default: 1000; typical values: 100-1000

oneOf.description:
HDR Histogram: records every latency with bounded relative error.
This is the default policy.

max_value_us.description:
Optional upper bound (in microseconds). When unset, the histogram
grows to fit every recorded value. When set, larger values are
recorded as this bound and counted in the `clamped_samples` output.

sigfigs.description:
Number of significant digits (1-5)
Higher = more accurate but more memory

bucket_duration.description: Time bucket duration for per-second per-connection records

include_records.description: Include per-second per-connection records in JSON output

sampling_policy.description:
Global latency sampling policy for the aggregated collector.
If unset, the first traffic group's policy is used (current behavior).
Set to "none" to disable global latency recording.

TimestampSourceConfig.description:
Source of a traffic group's send and receive timestamps

Every timestamp holds the user-space cycles read when its send or
receive call completed. Kernel and NIC timestamps come in addition, and
a latency uses them when its send and its receive both have one from the
same clock, which splits its round trip in the latency breakdown.

oneOf.description: User-space cycle counts only (default)
Kernel software timestamps (SO_TIMESTAMPING) of every send and receive

NIC hardware timestamps of this interface, which must already have
hardware timestamping switched on: the run fails otherwise, and never
switches it on or falls back to another source

The NIC timestamps of a user-space stack that owns the NIC (transport
"ntcp" with backend "dpdk"): RX hardware timestamps converted to the
user-space clock, and the time the stack queued each request to the
NIC

on_error.description:
What an error reply (a Redis error, an HTTP 4xx or 5xx, ...) does:
"count" it in `requests.errors` (default), or "abort" the run

protocol.description: Protocol for this group (redis, memcached-binary, memcached-ascii, http, masstree, dns, nvme-tcp, xylem-echo)

protocol_config.description:
Protocol-specific configuration as a JSON value.
Each protocol factory interprets this according to its own schema.
The core is protocol-agnostic - this value is passed directly to the protocol factory.

request_timeout.description:
How long a request may wait for its response before it times out,
frees its pipeline slot, and counts as timed out without a latency
(e.g., "500ms"). Only for transport "udp", where it defaults to 1s;
stream transports retransmit and never time out requests.

target.description: Target address for this group (e.g., "127.0.0.1:6379" or "/var/run/redis.sock")

threads.description: Thread IDs this group runs on

timestamps.description:
Source of the send and receive timestamps latencies are measured
with: "user" (default), "kernel", or { hardware = "<interface>" }.
Only for transports "tcp" and "udp" on Linux; traffic groups that
share a thread must use the same source.

transport.description: Transport layer: tcp, udp, unix (defaults to "tcp")

ValidityCheck.description: Checks that a run applied its configured load

oneOf.description: Fraction of a rate-driven group's intended sends that never went out
Fraction of a rate-driven group's sends that went out late

ValidityConfig.description:
Checks that a run applied the load it was configured with. Each applies
to every traffic group with a rate-driven traffic policy; a closed loop
has no schedule to fall behind.

enabled.description: Run the checks (default true). With false, a run is never invalid.

max_late_send_ratio.description:
Largest fraction of a group's sent requests that may lag their
intended send time by more than 100 µs (default 0.01)

max_unsent_ratio.description:
Largest fraction of a group's intended sends (`sent + unsent`) that may
remain unsent at the end of the window (default 0.001)
